### Getting started

#### Read

Read the work as it stands:

- The full paper (background, methods, results, discussion) is in [report/manuscript.qmd](./report/manuscript.qmd), which assembles the section files in [report/quarto/](./report/quarto/).
- The supplement is assembled from fragments in [report/quarto/supplement/](./report/quarto/supplement/); [report/supplement.qmd](./report/supplement.qmd) combines them into a single PDF, and [report/supplement/](./report/supplement/) renders them as separate website pages.
- The former pre-print is on [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.04.10.25325611); note, this is out of date.
  - See an [overview of what's changed](submission/development-since-first-submission.md)

#### Explore

A guide to the codebase:

- `R/` --- analysis and utility scripts:
  - `process-score.R` scores forecasts; `process-data.R` joins scores to explanatory variables; `analysis-model.R` fits the GAMM; `analysis-descriptive.R` builds summary tables; `plot-model-results.R` and `plot-model-flow.R` make the figures; `dag-check.R` defines the confounding DAG.
  - `analysis-supplement.R` builds the supplement's descriptive tables and figures.
  - `utils-data.R`, `utils-metadata.R`, `utils-variants.R` --- data access, model metadata, and variant-phase classification; `utils-effects.R` extracts effects and contrasts from the fitted GAMM.
  - `R/sensitivity/` --- robustness checks (response family, family by interaction, horizon specification, link function, autocorrelation).
  - `diy-model.qmd` and `utils-diy.R` refit the GAMM under your own specification (see [Try a model spec](#try-a-model-spec)).
  - See [R/README](R/README.md) for inputs, outputs, and data flow.
- `data/` --- forecasts (`covid19-forecast-hub-europe.parquet`), observed incidence, populations, model classification, and computed scores.
- `report/quarto/` --- the manuscript section files; `report/quarto/supplement/` the supplement.
- `output/` --- fitted model results and diagnostic plots, under scale-named subdirectories (`log/`, `natural/`).

#### Reproduce

To re-run the analysis end to end:

1. Restore the package environment ([renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html)):

   ```{r}
      renv::restore()
   ```

2. Data is already in `data/`.
   To re-download it from public sources, see the [data/README](data/README.md).

3. Score forecasts on the log and natural scales (writes to `data/`):

   ```{r}
      library(here)
      source(here("R", "process-score.R"))
   ```

4. Assemble scores with explanatory variables:

   ```{r}
      source(here("R", "process-data.R"))
   ```

5. Fit the GAMM to the weighted interval score, once per scoring scale (writes to `output/log/` and `output/natural/`).
   Sourcing the script only defines `model_wis()`; the calls do the fitting, and take several minutes each.

   ```{r}
      source(here("R", "analysis-model.R"))
      model_wis(scoring_scale = "log", output_dir = here("output", "log"),
                spec_label = "primary-fs")
      model_wis(scoring_scale = "natural", output_dir = here("output", "natural"),
                spec_label = "primary-fs")
   ```

6. Render the manuscript, or the full site (manuscript, supplement PDF, and supplement pages):

   ```sh
      quarto render index.qmd   # manuscript only
      quarto render             # manuscript + supplement PDF + supplement pages
   ```

   Render `index.qmd`, not `report/manuscript.qmd`: the latter's includes are project-root-relative and only resolve when a file at the repo root is the top-level document.

   Run `model_wis()` before rendering. The results section reads `output/log/results.rds` and does not refit.

#### Try a model spec

To see how the estimates move when the model changes, open [R/diy-model.qmd](R/diy-model.qmd).
It refits the GAMM on a within-model subsample of the saved analysis data (about a minute per fit), and compares effects across specifications: adjustment set, scoring scale, response family, and horizon term.
Edit the `update()` calls to try your own.
